source_text: Ἐπιζητεῖ δὲ ὁ λόγος, εἰ συγκατεσκευάσθη τῷ κόσμῳ τὸ σκότος, καὶ εἰ ἀρχαιότερον τοῦ φωτὸς, καὶ διὰ τί τὸ χεῖρον πρεσβύτερον; Λέγομεν τοίνυν καὶ τοῦτο τὸ σκότος μὴ κατ' οὐσίαν ὑφεστη κέναι, ἀλλὰ πάθος εἶναι περὶ τὸν ἀέρα στερήσει φωτὸς ἐπιγινόμενον. Ποίου τοίνυν φωτὸς ἄμοιρος αἰφνιδίως ὁ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τόπος εὑρέθη, ὥστε τὸ σκότος ἐπάνω εἶναι τοῦ ὕδατος; Λογιζόμεθα τοίνυν ὅτι, εἴπερ τι ἦν πρὸ τῆς τοῦ αἰσθητοῦ τούτου καὶ φθαρτοῦ κόσμου συστάσεως, ἐν φωτὶ ἂν ἦν δηλονότι. Οὔτε γὰρ αἱ τῶν ἀγγέλων ἀξίαι, οὔτε πᾶσαι αἱ ἐπουράνιοι στρατιαὶ, οὔτε ὅλως εἴ τι ἐστὶν ὠνομασμένον ἢ ἀκατονόμαστον τῶν λογικῶν φύσεων, καὶ τῶν λειτουργικῶν πνευμάτων ἐν σκότῳ διῆγεν, ἀλλ' ἐν φωτὶ καὶ πάσῃ εὐφρο σύνῃ πνευματικῇ τὴν πρέπουσαν ἑαυτοῖς κατάστασιν εἶχε. Καὶ τούτοις οὐδεὶς ἀντερεῖ, οὔκουν ὅστις γε τὸ ὑπερουράνιον φῶς ἐν ταῖς τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἐπαγγελίαις ἐκδέχεται, περὶ οὗ Σολομών φησι· Φῶς δικαίοις διὰ παντός· καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος· Εὐχαριστοῦντες Πατρὶ τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῇ μερίδι τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί. Εἰ γὰρ οἱ καταδικαζόμενοι πέμπονται εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον, δηλονότι οἱ τὰ τῆς ἀποδοχῆς ἄξια εἰργασμένοι, ἐν τῷ ὑπερκοσμίῳ φωτὶ τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν ἔχουσιν. Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐγένετο ὁ οὐρανὸς προστάγματι Θεοῦ ἀθρόως περιταθεὶς τοῖς ἐντὸς ὑπὸ τῆς οἰκείας αὐτοῦ περιφερείας ἀπειλημμένοις, σῶμα ἔχων συνεχὲς, ἱκανὸν τῶν ἔξω διαστῆσαι τὰ ἔνδον, ἀναγκαίως τὸν ἐναπολειφθέντα αὐτῷ τόπον ἀφεγγῆ κατέστησε, τὴν ἔξωθεν αὐγὴν διακόψας. Τρία γὰρ δεῖ συνδραμεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς σκιᾶς, τὸ φῶς, τὸ σῶμα, τὸν ἀλαμπῆ τόπον. Τὸ τοίνυν ἐγκόσμιον σκότος τῇ σκιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανίου σώματος παρυπέστη. Νόησον δέ μοι ἀπὸ παραδείγματος ἐναργοῦς τὸ λεγόμενον, ἐν σταθηρᾷ μεσημβρίᾳ σκηνήν τινα ἐκ πυκνῆς καὶ στεγανῆς ὕλης ἑαυτῷ περιστήσαντα, καὶ ἐν σκότῳ αὐτοσχεδίῳ ἑαυτὸν καθειργνύντα. Τοιοῦτον οὖν κἀκεῖνο τὸ σκότος ὑπόθου, οὐ προηγουμένως ὑφεστηκὸς, ἀλλ' ἐπακολουθῆσαν ἑτέροις. Τοῦτο δὴ τὸ σκότος καὶ ἐπιβαίνειν λέγεται τῇ ἀβύσσῳ, ἐπειδὴ τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀέρος πέφυκε ταῖς ἐπιφανείαις τῶν σωμάτων συνάπτεσθαι. Τότε δὲ ὕδωρ ἦν τοῖς πᾶσιν ἐπιπολάζον. Διόπερ ἀναγκαίως τὸ σκότος ἐπάνω ὑπάρχειν εἴρηται τῆς ἀβύσσου. 2.6 Καὶ Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ, φησὶν, ἐπεφέρετο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος. Εἴτε τοῦτο λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα, τοῦ ἀέρος τὴν χύσιν, δέξαι τὰ μέρη τοῦ κόσμου καταριθμοῦντά σοι τὸν συγγραφέα, ὅτι ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς οὐρανὸν, γῆν, ὕδωρ, ἀέρα, καὶ τοῦτον χεόμενον ἤδη καὶ ῥέοντα. Εἴτε, ὃ καὶ μᾶλλον ἀληθέστερόν ἐστι καὶ τοῖς πρὸ ἡμῶν ἐγκριθὲν, Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ, τὸ ἅγιον εἴρηται· διὰ τὸ τετηρῆσθαι τοῦτο ἰδιαζόντως καὶ ἐξαιρέτως τῆς τοιαύτης μνήμης ὑπὸ τῆς Γραφῆς ἀξιοῦ σθαι, καὶ μηδὲν ἄλλο Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ, ἢ τὸ ἅγιον τὸ τῆς θείας καὶ μακαρίας Τριάδος συμπληρωτικὸν ὀνομάζεσθαι. Καὶ ταύτην προσδεξάμενος τὴν διάνοιαν, μείζονα τὴν ἀπ' αὐτῆς ὠφέλειαν εὑρήσεις. Πῶς οὖν ἐπεφέρετο τοῦτο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος; Ἐρῶ σοι οὐκ ἐμαυτοῦ λόγον, ἀλλὰ Σύρου ἀνδρὸς σοφίας κοσμικῆς τοσοῦτον ἀφεστηκότος, ὅσον ἐγγὺς ἦν τῆς τῶν ἀληθινῶν ἐπιστήμης. Ἔλεγε τοίνυν τὴν τῶν Σύρων φωνὴν ἐμφατικωτέραν τε εἶναι, καὶ διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὴν Ἑβραΐδα γειτνίασιν, μᾶλλόν πως τῇ ἐννοίᾳ τῶν Γραφῶν προσεγγίζειν.
orientation: Basil is answering the question of whether darkness existed before light and what darkness is, continuing his literal reading of Genesis 1:2.
pass_a_gloss: The argument seeks, whether darkness was co-established with the world, and whether it is older than light, and why the worse is older? We say then that this darkness also did not subsist according to substance, but is an affection around the air, coming upon it by deprivation of light. Of what light then was the place in the world suddenly found without share, so that darkness was upon the water? We reason then that, if anything was before the constitution of this perceptible and corruptible world, it was clearly in light. For neither the ranks of the angels, nor all the heavenly armies, nor in general if anything is named or unnamed of the rational natures, and of the ministering spirits, passed its time in darkness, but in light and all spiritual gladness it had the condition fitting for itself. And no one will contradict these things, at least not whoever awaits the supercelestial light in the promises of the good things, about which Solomon says: Light is always for the righteous; and the apostle: Giving thanks to the Father who made us sufficient for the share of the lot of the saints in the light. For if those being condemned are sent into the outer darkness, clearly those who have done things worthy of acceptance have their rest in the supercosmic light. Since then the heaven came to be by the command of God, suddenly stretched around the things within, enclosed by its own circumference, having a continuous body, able to separate the things inside from the things outside, necessarily it made the place left remaining within it lightless, cutting off the brightness from outside. For three things must come together for a shadow: the light, the body, the lightless place. The cosmic darkness then came to subsist by the shadow of the heavenly body. Understand for me the thing said from a clear example: at still midday someone setting up around himself a tent from dense and watertight material, and shutting himself in self-made darkness. Such then suppose that darkness also to be, not subsisting primarily, but following upon other things. This darkness is also said to walk upon the deep, since the extremities of the air are by nature joined to the surfaces of bodies. And at that time water was spread over all things. Therefore necessarily darkness is said to be upon the deep. 2.6 And the Spirit of God, it says, was borne upon the water. If this says the spirit, the pouring of the air, receive the writer enumerating for you the parts of the world, that God made heaven, earth, water, air, and this already being poured and flowing. If, which is also more true and approved by those before us, the Spirit of God, the Holy One, is meant: because this has been kept specially and exceptionally worthy of such mention by Scripture, and no other Spirit of God is named than the Holy One, the completing one of the divine and blessed Trinity. And having accepted this meaning, you will find greater benefit from it. How then was this borne upon the water? I will tell you not my own word, but of a Syrian man who stood as far from worldly wisdom as he was near to the knowledge of true things. He said then that the Syrian tongue is more expressive, and because of its nearness to the Hebrew, somehow approaches more closely to the meaning of the Scriptures.

choices.term: πάθος εἶναι περὶ τὸν ἀέρα στερήσει φωτὸς ἐπιγινόμενον
choices.english: an affection around the air, coming upon it by deprivation of light
choices.why: Keeps the philosophical precision: darkness is not a substance but a state (pathos) of the air caused by absence of light.
rejected: a condition of the air resulting from the absence of light
a quality in the air produced by lack of light

choices.term: ἐν φωτὶ καὶ πάσῃ εὐφροσύνῃ πνευματικῇ
choices.english: in light and all spiritual gladness
choices.why: Preserves the pairing of light with spiritual joy as the proper state of angelic beings.
rejected: in light and every spiritual delight
in light and complete spiritual happiness

choices.term: τῇ σκιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανίου σώματος παρυπέστη
choices.english: came to subsist by the shadow of the heavenly body
choices.why: The verb paruphistemi means to come into being as a by-product or accompaniment, which is Basil's key point that darkness is derivative, not primary.
rejected: came into existence through the shadow

choices.why: The glossary does not cover this verb; 'borne upon' preserves the motion sense of epipherō and matches Basil's later discussion of the Syriac nuance.
Basil uses a technical Trinitarian term: the Spirit completes the Trinity. 'Completing one' keeps the participial force.
Emphatikos here means capable of conveying meaning more forcefully or vividly, not 'emphatic' in the modern sense.

pass_b_english: But the argument presses further: was darkness created along with the world? Is it older than light? And why is the worse thing the more ancient? And why is the worse thing the more ancient? We answer that this darkness did not subsist in its own right as a substance. It is an affection around the air, coming upon it by deprivation of light. What light, then, did the region within the world suddenly find itself without, so that darkness came to be over the water? We reason as follows: if anything existed before the constitution of this perceptible and perishable world, it was clearly in light. For neither the ranks of the angels, nor all the heavenly armies, nor any named or unnamed rational nature or ministering spirit whatsoever, lived in darkness. They held their proper state in light and all spiritual gladness. No one will dispute this—at least no one who awaits the light above the heavens in the promises of good things, about which Solomon says, “Light is always for the righteous” (Proverbs 13:9), and the apostle says, “Giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified us to share in the inheritance of the saints in light” (Colossians 1:12). For if those who are condemned are sent into the outer darkness, then clearly those who have done what is worthy of acceptance have their rest in the light beyond the world.

So when the heaven came into being by God’s command, suddenly stretched around, enclosing the things within by its own circumference—a continuous body able to separate what is inside from what is outside—it necessarily made the space left within it lightless, cutting off the brightness from outside. For three things must come together for a shadow: the light, the body, and the unlit place. The darkness within the world, then, came to subsist by the shadow of the heavenly body. Understand what I am saying from a clear example: at a still midday, someone sets up a tent around himself made of dense, watertight material and shuts himself inside in a makeshift darkness. Suppose that the darkness in question was like that—not subsisting in its own right beforehand, but following upon other things.

This darkness is also said to walk upon the deep, because the outermost part of the air naturally touches the surfaces of bodies. At that time water lay over everything. Therefore it is necessarily said that darkness was over the deep.

“And the Spirit of God,” it says, “was borne upon the water” (Genesis 1:2). If this means the spirit as the pouring of the air, then accept that the writer is enumerating for you the parts of the world: God made heaven, earth, water, air—and this air already being poured out and flowing. But if—what is more true and was approved by those before us—the Spirit of God means the Holy Spirit, then accept this reading, because Scripture especially and uniquely honors the Spirit with this mention, and nothing else is called the Spirit of God except the Holy Spirit, the completing element of the divine and blessed Trinity. If you accept this meaning, you will find the benefit from it greater.

How, then, was this Spirit borne upon the water? I will tell you not my own word, but that of a Syrian man who was as far from worldly wisdom as he was near to the knowledge of true things. He said that the Syriac language is more expressive, and because of its closeness to Hebrew it somehow approaches the meaning of the Scriptures more nearly.

problems.why: συμπληρωτικὸν is adjectival ('the completing [element/member]'), not a nominalized 'one.'
problems.fix: the completing element of the divine and blessed Trinity

problems.ruling: αὐτοσχεδίῳ means 'improvised/hastily'; 'self-made' risks misreading as self-created, misleading.

last_rejected.why: 'Walk upon' suggests treading; Greek means 'come upon, be upon' the deep.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιβαίνειν means 'walk/tread upon'; within normal range for 'be upon.' Not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Completing element' is vague; Greek means 'what completes/fills out' the Trinity.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ συμπληρωτικὸν = 'completing/filling'; 'completing element' conveys this adequately. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: 'Was borne' is passive; Greek middle suggests 'was hovering/moving over' (traditional rendering).
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπεφέρετο can mean 'was borne upon'; standard rendering of Gen 1:2. Mere preference, not major error.
